articles.title: Show HN: Mason – a lightweight Postgres read-replica, built on columnar storage
articles.excerpt: Hi HN! TLDR: we’ve built an open-source drop-in replacement for a postgres read-replica, powered by duckdb’s columnar compute engine. It’s very fast. And it looks like postgres. So, this started out as: let’s just connect Clickhouse to our postgres dbs and throw our analytics queries at it instead. That will speed everything up. But we quickly found that 1) Clickhouse comes with quite the learning curve (engine optimisation) to make it fast (we needed something we could easily drop in to any customer’s postgres scenario), and 2) we had underestimated how different clickhouse’s SQL syntax was to postgres. Don’t get me wrong: we love Clickhouse (it’s ridiculously fast if you know what queries to expect), it just didn’t work for our ad-hoc postgres workloads. So we went searching for alternatives that were 1) more plug-and-play and 2) looked a lot more like postgres. We dismissed a bunch based on desk research alone: - pg_mooncake (seems to have stalled since data bricks bought them) - pg_duckdb (seems to offer fast queries, or fresh data, but not both - we needed both) - materialize/risingwave/readyset (like Clickhouse, they require knowing the query shapes upfront - not ideal for ad-hoc workloads) - firebolt (license makes it challenging to offer to our customers) - redshift / alloydb / etc (we wanted something cloud-provider agnostic) And we shortlisted 3: - pg_clickhouse (Postgres extension that parses SQL in Postgres and pushes the work down to ClickHouse) - cedarDB (closed-source, Postgres-compatible analytical database) - duckdb (open-source, embedded columnar analytics engine with a Postgres-like SQL dialect) We needed to know how they would perform on real postgres queries, so we took a backlog of 5,410 (hand-written) queries (chosen because they had been slow to execute against postgres) from 159 real postgres databases. We then generated synthetic data (dynamically using the schemas from those 159 databases) to fill 159 local databases so
articles.summary: Mason propose un réplica PostgreSQL léger en stockage colonne via DuckDB, compatible et rapide pour les requêtes analytiques ad-hoc.

articles.title: GitLab Dedicated: A go-live guide
articles.excerpt: GitLab Dedicated is a single-tenant SaaS solution that is fully isolated, deployed in your preferred AWS cloud region, and hosted and maintained by GitLab. GitLab Dedicated and compliance covers why regulated organizations choose a single-tenant instance operated by GitLab, and serves as a starting point for evaluation. In this article, you'll learn what to do after you sign on to GitLab Dedicated, including understanding which responsibilities GitLab takes on and which remain with your teams, as well as what controls each team needs to put in place. Teams arriving from any self-managed source-control or CI/CD platform bring an operating model built around upgrade runbooks, pre-flight checks, staging environments, and rollback plans. On GitLab Dedicated, many of those responsibilities move to GitLab, and the ones that stay with you look different. Division of responsibility GitLab Dedicated splits platform operation between GitLab and the customer. GitLab owns You own Version validation and testing Pipeline configuration Security patching Scripts and services calling the GitLab API Database migrations Webhooks and integrations Monitoring and observability Runner configuration Backup and regional recovery Migration away from deprecated features The right-hand column is where most of your team's work now sits. GitLab operates the platform. Your teams operate what runs on it. What you configure in Switchboard Switchboard is the administration portal for GitLab Dedicated. From there, you manage: IP allowlists for inbound access SAML and instance authentication Operational email addresses Access to your application logs, which GitLab delivers to a private Amazon S3 bucket AWS PrivateLink connections and bring-your-own-key encryption Hosted runners Switchboard has two roles: Admin edits instance configuration and manages Switchboard users; Read-only views instance data. Some capabilities must be enabled on your tenant by GitLab before they appear in Switchboard. If an opt
articles.summary: GitLab Dedicated externalise la gestion de la plateforme SaaS en mode single-tenant, réduisant les tâches d'exploitation pour les équipes.

articles.title: Human in the Loop with Spring AI 2.1: Tool Calls That Survive a Restart
articles.excerpt: Spring AI: Tool Call Confirmation | Session Extensions | Demo A bank support agent can look up why a mortgage payment failed. That is reading, and the model may do it on its own. Collecting the payment today moves money, and a person must approve it first. Asking "may I?" is the easy part. The hard part is the wait. The approver answers minutes or hours later, maybe on another instance of the application, maybe after a restart. Whatever the agent was doing must still be there when the answer comes. In Spring AI 2.0, approving a tool call meant user-controlled tool execution : you switch the tool loop off and run every round yourself. That is a lot to take over for one call. Spring AI 2.1 adds tool call confirmation : you mark a tool, and the loop runs the harmless tools as before and pauses only when the model asks for a marked one. The 2.1.0 GA announcement covered it in one paragraph. This post shows how it works, and how the new community project Spring AI Session Extensions keeps the pause in the session log, so that another process can resume it. Mark the tool The mark goes on the tool. This is the mortgage service of the demo, an ordinary Spring @Service : @Tool(description = "Returns the customer's mortgage payments for one month: due date, amount in CHF, status and, " + "for a failed payment, the reason.") public String mortgagePaymentStatus(@ToolParam(description = "The month, as YYYY-MM") String month, ToolContext toolContext) { ... } // This call moves money, so a person approves it first @Tool(description = "Collects the planned retry of a failed mortgage payment today instead of on its planned " + "date. It debits the customer's account.", requiresConfirmation = true) public String retryMortgagePaymentNow(@ToolParam(description = "The month of the payment, as YYYY-MM") String month, ToolContext toolContext) { ... } The first tool runs as before. A call of the second one pauses the loop. The annotation is the default rule. Two more ways cover the cases i

articles.title: Amazon EC2 X8i instances are now available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region
articles.excerpt: Starting today, Amazon Elastic Compute Cloud (Amazon EC2) X8i instances are available in the Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region. These instances are powered by custom Intel Xeon 6 processors available only on AWS. X8i instances are SAP-certified and deliver the highest performance and fastest memory bandwidth among comparable Intel processors in the cloud. They deliver up to 43% higher performance, 1.5x more memory capacity (up to 6TB), and 3.3x more memory bandwidth compared to previous generation X2i instances. X8i instances are designed for memory-intensive workloads like SAP HANA, large databases, data analytics, and Electronic Design Automation (EDA). Compared to X2i instances, X8i instances offer up to 50% higher SAPS performance, up to 47% faster PostgreSQL performance, 88% faster Memcached performance, and 46% faster AI inference performance. X8i instances come in 14 sizes, from large to 96xlarge, including two bare metal options. To get started, visit the AWS Management Console . X8i instances can be purchased via Savings Plans, On-Demand instances, and Spot instances. For more information visit X8i instances page .
articles.summary: Amazon EC2 X8i instances, avec processeurs Intel Xeon 6, sont désormais disponibles en Nouvelle-Zélande, offrant jusqu'à 43% de performance en plus et 6 To de mémoire.

articles.title: AWS Sign-In introduces configurable Sign-in duration of up to 90 days
articles.excerpt: AWS Sign-In now enables developers and AI agents to stay authenticated for up to 90 days without frequent sign-ins or consent prompts. With this launch, administrators can configure Sign-in duration , which controls how long an OAuth Sign-in session remains active, for individual IAM users and roles. This capability reduces authentication interruptions for long-running workflows and provides a more secure alternative to static access keys by using short-lived, renewable credentials. Existing session duration limits remain unchanged unless administrators explicitly configure longer durations. Sign-In Duration supports AWS CLI (aws login), AWS MCP Server, and other OAuth-enabled applications. It does not affect AWS Management Console sessions. Customers can configure the setting using the IAM console, AWS CLI, or IAM API in all AWS commercial Regions. To learn more , see the AWS Sign-In session management User Guide , Configure Sign-In duration on Role User Guid e, Condition Key User Guide
articles.summary: AWS Sign-In permet désormais des sessions OAuth jusqu'à 90 jours pour les workflows longs, réduisant les interruptions d'authentification.

articles.title: Amazon API Gateway announces API Portal
articles.excerpt: Today, Amazon API Gateway announces API Portal , a new feature that discovers, governs, and documents the APIs and AI endpoints behind Amazon API Gateway, Application Load Balancer, and Amazon CloudFront across your AWS organization. Many organizations can't see which APIs are running, which were never registered, which are no longer maintained, and which lack protection. API Portal builds a continuously updated inventory using AWS-side traffic logs and service configuration records, with nothing to install, no logs to forward, and no traffic to reroute, for a single account or your entire AWS organization. Every discovered API starts as a shadow API until you choose to manage it. API Portal labels each API as public or private and identifies AI endpoints, including MCP servers, A2A servers, and LLM endpoints. For managed APIs, it flags those that stop receiving traffic or lose their owner and evaluates security posture against best practices such as authentication, throttling, and AWS WAF protection. With AWS WAF API Security , it also shows the security events detected per API. You can publish any managed API in a documentation portal for internal teams or external partners, with your branding, Amazon Cognito access control, and interactive Try it pages. If you already use API Gateway Portals, your portals continue to work and are now managed from the Documentation Portals section of API Portal. API Portal is available in 32 AWS Regions; see the Amazon API Gateway FAQ and pricing pages for details. To get started, see the following resources: Amazon API Gateway product page Introducing API and AI security on AWS blog API Portal documentation AWS WAF API Security documentation
articles.summary: Amazon API Gateway lance API Portal pour inventorier, sécuriser et documenter automatiquement les APIs et endpoints IA dans toute l'organisation AWS.

articles.title: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports managed observability and user management extensions for Slurm clusters
articles.excerpt: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod now supports managed cluster extensions for Slurm clusters. You can install, configure, update, and remove managed features through the SageMaker AI console or API. The first two extensions cover observability and user management. Earlier, every observability or user management change for HyperPod Slurm clusters meant editing lifecycle scripts and then replacing or rerunning nodes. Now, HyperPod manages these features for you, and you keep lifecycle scripts and custom AMIs for your organization's own software. For each extension, you declare a configuration. HyperPod validates it and applies it to every node, including nodes you add later. It then reports the extension's status and the health of each node. The observability extension collects node, GPU, Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA), Slurm job, and Slurm cluster metrics. It sends them to Amazon CloudWatch or Amazon Managed Service for Prometheus, and you can add Amazon Managed Grafana dashboards. The user management extension creates users and groups with the same IDs on every node. It also controls who can sign in with SSH and use sudo on each node type, with local users, Active Directory, or both. Cluster extensions are available at no additional charge in all AWS Regions where Amazon SageMaker HyperPod is available. You pay only for the AWS resources you use. To learn more, see Cluster extensions in the Amazon SageMaker AI Developer Guide, read the launch blog , or visit the Amazon SageMaker HyperPod product page .
articles.summary: Amazon SageMaker HyperPod automatise l'observabilité et la gestion des utilisateurs pour les clusters Slurm, simplifiant leur maintenance et leur supervision.

articles.title: Amazon OpenSearch Service now supports OpenSearch version 3.9
articles.excerpt: You can now run OpenSearch version 3.9 on Amazon OpenSearch Service. OpenSearch 3.9 helps you reduce vector memory and storage, evaluate search quality with more large language model (LLM) providers, build more responsive AI agents, and control access to shared resources. This release adds a new half-float vector type and a bf16 encoder, which store each vector dimension in 16 bits to reduce the memory and storage your vector indexes need. New 2-bit and 4-bit scalar quantization lets you choose the right balance of compression and recall for each workload. Base64-encoded vector ingestion makes request payloads smaller, which speeds up bulk loading. In addition, radial search now uses a redesigned graph traversal to improve both recall and throughput. In Search Relevance Workbench, LLM-as-a-Judge now works with Amazon Bedrock and other LLM providers through ML Commons connectors. You can also retry failed documents, edit ratings, and reuse earlier judgments to reduce repeated LLM calls. OpenSearch 3.9 also adds gRPC streaming for model predictions and agent execution. Responses come back token by token, so your agentic applications can show answers as they’re generated. Finally, the new resource sharing and access control framework allows you to share resources such as anomaly detectors and machine learning models with specific users and roles without granting broad access. OpenSearch 3.9 is available in all AWS Regions where Amazon OpenSearch Service is offered. To learn how to upgrade, see Upgrading Amazon OpenSearch Service domains in the Amazon OpenSearch Service Developer Guide.
articles.summary: Amazon OpenSearch Service supporte désormais OpenSearch 3.9 avec compression vectorielle, LLM étendu et contrôle d'accès granulaire.

articles.title: AWS WAF introduces simplified pricing
articles.excerpt: AWS WAF now offers simplified pricing that follows what you protect instead of how you configure it. Previously, you paid separate charges for each web ACL, rule, rule group subscription, and capacity tier, making every security decision a billing calculation. Now, your bill follows three dimensions: the resources you protect, the traffic AWS WAF inspects, and the level of protection you apply. This makes the cost-benefit trade-off easy to understand, and adding or changing rules no longer changes your rate. This new pricing goes into effect on Feb 1, 2027. The new model makes protection costs predictable before you deploy. Each web ACL now includes up to 2,500 WCU at no extra charge, up from 1,500, and you can add rules such as Bot Control common protections or the Anti-DDoS rule group without additional fees. You pay a resource fee for each protected resource, a base request fee for every request AWS WAF inspects, and a premium request fee only for traffic evaluated by advanced protections like Bot Control targeted protections, Fraud Control, API Security, and AI Security. AWS WAF's new pricing is effective from Feb 1, 2027 in all AWS commercial Regions, including Cape Town, Hong Kong, Hyderabad, Jakarta, Malaysia, Melbourne, Mumbai, New Zealand, Osaka, Seoul, Singapore, Sydney, Taipei, Thailand, Tokyo, Calgary, Frankfurt, Ireland, London, Milan, Paris, Spain, Stockholm, Zurich, Tel Aviv, Sao Paulo, N. Virginia, Ohio, N. California, Oregon, as well as in AWS GovCloud, China Regions, and AWS Isolated Regions. To learn more, visit the AWS WAF pricing page and review the AWS WAF Developer Guide as well as the blog post AWS WAF pricing now follows what you protect, not how you configure it .
articles.summary: AWS WAF simplifie sa tarification en 2027 : coût basé sur les ressources protégées et le trafic inspecté, avec des protections avancées payantes.

themes.trend: GitLab Dedicated externalise la gestion des plateformes SaaS en mode single-tenant, réduisant les tâches d'exploitation pour les équipes DevOps.

dynamicThemes.label: Mises à jour critiques de logiciels
dynamicThemes.trend: Plusieurs correctifs de sécurité majeurs sont publiés aujourd'hui pour Grafana (versions 13.x et 12.x) et Traefik (v3.x et v2.x), ciblant des CVE critiques identiques. Ces mises à jour s'accompagnent d'améliorations fonctionnelles comme la gestion des identités ou la compatibilité Kubernetes, reflétant une priorité absolue sur la sécurité et la stabilité des plateformes.

dynamicThemes.label: Actualités hors périmètre technique
dynamicThemes.trend: Plusieurs articles relèvent de l'actualité générale ou culturelle, comme l'élection du mot de l'année 2026 par le Macquarie Dictionary ou des sujets sociétaux comme la musique générée par IA ou les villes 'aimables'. Ces éléments, bien que non techniques, reflètent des tendances sociétales influençant indirectement l'écosystème tech.

dynamicThemes.label: Observabilité et télémétrie
dynamicThemes.trend: OpenTelemetry continue d'évoluer avec des versions nightly du Collector et de ses outils associés (opampsupervisor, builder), intégrant des corrections et optimisations. Ces mises à jour visent à renforcer la collecte et l'analyse des métriques, traces et logs, essentiels pour le monitoring des infrastructures modernes.

dynamicThemes.label: Sécurité réseau et confidentialité
dynamicThemes.trend: AstridVPN propose un VPN sans logs ni identification, tandis qu'une campagne cyber attaque cible des serveurs Check Point dans 22 organisations. Ces événements illustrent l'intensification des menaces et l'importance des solutions de confidentialité et de protection des infrastructures critiques.

dynamicThemes.label: Bases de données et stockage
dynamicThemes.trend: Mason introduit un réplica PostgreSQL léger en stockage colonne via DuckDB, optimisé pour les requêtes analytiques ad-hoc. Par ailleurs, Amazon OpenSearch Service supporte désormais OpenSearch 3.9 avec des fonctionnalités avancées comme la compression vectorielle et le contrôle d'accès granulaire, reflétant une évolution vers des bases de données plus performantes et sécurisées.

dynamicThemes.label: Observabilité système et performances
dynamicThemes.trend: Brendan Gregg reste une référence incontournable avec ses méthodes d'analyse des performances système, tandis que des outils comme Jetty Pro optimisent les serveurs web pour des charges critiques. Ces évolutions soulignent l'importance croissante de l'observabilité fine pour garantir la résilience des infrastructures.

dynamicThemes.label: Incidents et pannes majeures
dynamicThemes.trend: Microsoft a déclaré un 'Code Red' après une panne historique impactant ses services cloud, soulignant la vulnérabilité des infrastructures critiques face aux incidents majeurs. Ces événements rappellent l'importance de la résilience et de la préparation aux pannes pour les équipes SRE.

dynamicThemes.label: Capacités et impacts de l'IA
dynamicThemes.trend: L'IA atteint en 2026 des capacités initialement prévues pour 2035, bouleversant les attentes technologiques. Les agents LLM servent désormais les intérêts de leurs entreprises mères plutôt que ceux des utilisateurs, marquant un tournant dans l'utilisation de l'IA.
